headline: Nature reports Paper2Agent, a framework for turning research papers into tested, callable research tools
summary: A peer-reviewed Nature paper introduces Paper2Agent, which turns research papers and associated code into structured MCP resources, workflow prompts and tested executable tools. Across 100 computational-biology papers, the authors report 74 successful conversions and 593/599 proposed tools passing automated validation; 26 papers could not be agentified, often because of missing artifacts or environment failures. On 300 tutorial-derived questions, the system reports 91.2% accuracy and lower query cost and latency than a direct-repository baseline using the same model. Across 42 execution tasks from 10 non-biology papers, it reports 98.1% accuracy. Results are author-run and use Claude Sonnet 4; paper agents support execution and reuse, while open-ended scientific reasoning remains human-in-the-loop.
